overall_summary: A neighbor's handheld phone observes an older woman approaching an ordinary suburban driveway gate while one large black bear already occupies the gate opening from the other side. The woman opens the gate, gestures for the bear to move, and walks around it while the bear remains calm.
tone: Unplanned real-life neighbor footage: ordinary, observational, awkward, and believable, never cinematic, staged, polished, promotional, or commercial.
capture_style: Consumer smartphone recording by an ordinary person, with natural exposure, imperfect framing, and subtle human handheld movement unless the shot explicitly requires a locked-off camera. No tripod or professional camera rig by default.
visual_style: Authentic neighbor-filmed smartphone video, medium-wide framing, natural late-afternoon daylight, ordinary suburban driveway, modest phone exposure and handheld imperfection, documentary realism.
visual_realism: Real-world documentary observation with natural light, ordinary locations, realistic motion, and no professional color grade or advertising polish.
audio_policy: Atmospheric location sound and physical foley only: sounds must come from the real environment or visible actions.
camera_lock: One completely locked-off viewpoint from the edge of the neighboring driveway. Keep the gate, driveway, path, woman, and bear spatially consistent across all panels. Remove all vehicles from the scene. No camera movement, camera cut, alternate angle, or change to a cinematic viewpoint.
continuity_invariants: Exactly one older woman and one large black bear remain the only characters in every frame.
The bear is already behind the closed gate in frame 1 and does not appear from nowhere.
The gate is closed through frame 2 and opens only through the woman's action beginning in frame 3.
The environment contains no vehicle or vehicle edge that could obstruct the locked-off composition.
The bear stays at the gate opening and does not teleport, duplicate, or enter a new location without a visible causal transition.

panel_convention: Six separate 16:9 landscape panels in a clean 2-by-3 storyboard sheet. Each panel has a white caption band beneath the image with its frame number and exact caption. Keep all text in the caption bands and never inside the image areas.
hard_constraints: Do not omit the bear from frame 1 or make it appear later without a causal entrance.
Do not show the gate open before frame 3.
In frame 3, the woman pulls the left gate toward the camera and away from the bear; never show her pushing the gate toward the bear.
Do not add extra people, duplicate bears, camera cuts, teleportation, morphing, or impossible movement.
Do not turn the storyboard sheet into a video frame, title card, or finished cinematic composition.
Do not show any vehicle, vehicle mirror, bumper, or vehicle edge in any frame.
Keep the camera viewpoint, horizon, gate posts, driveway edges, and background geometry fixed across all six panels.
